To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the liquid thermal conductivity of HFO and HCFO refrigerants can be predicted with an average absolute deviation (AAD) of 1.99% using a new correlation proposed in this work.
a new literature survey on thermal conductivity of low global warming potential (GWP) refrigerants in the liquid phase was carried out.
A new correlation is proposed for the liquid thermal conductivity of environmentally friendly refrigerants in the range from 0 to 0.7 of reduced temperature and up to 70 bar of pressure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the thermal conductivity correlations in the reduced temperature and pressure ranges 0.4–0.9 and up to 70 at 1 MPa.
a literature survey on the liquid thermal conductivity of HFOs and HCFOs in the reduced pressure range from 1 to 1.5.
the thermal conductivity of low global warming potential (GWP) refrigerants in the temperature range of reduced temperatures between 0.4 and 0.9, from saturation line to high pressure (up to 70 bar).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

Di Nicola et Al. (2014b) and Latini and Sotit (2012) correlations are the best available for liquid thermal conductivity prediction of low GWP alternative refrigerants in the temperature range 0–70 °C and up to 70 bar.
Di Nicola et Al. (2014b) equation is the best correlation for liquid thermal conductivity in the reduced temperature region 0.4–0.9 and for pressures lower than 70 MP.

the Di Nicola et Al. (2014) correlation, which has been re-fitted and adapted to low GWP refrigerant fluids, can be used with a good accuracy in the reduced temperature and pressure ranges of the present work.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the proposed equations are valid from the saturation line to the maximum pressure considered, i.e. up to 70  MPa, for reduced pressures lower or equal to 1, and for temperatures in the reduced range from 0,4 to 0,9.
the new correlations are able to describe the experimental data with good accuracy.
the proposed correlations can be applied to the liquid thermal conductivity of the six alternative refrigerants in the pressure range up to 70  MPa and in the temperature range 0 to 100  °C.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the thermal conductivity of the low GWP refrigerant is strongly dependent on the reduced temperature and pressure.
the thermal conductivity of alternative refrigerants is strongly dependent on the pressure.
the liquid thermal conductivity data for HFOs and HCFOs are scarce in the literature.
